title: With days to go before the midterms, data shows the U.S. economy is doing well
summary:
With days to go before the midterms, data shows the U.S. economy is doing welltoggle caption i Joe Raedle/Getty Images North AmericaThe U.S. economy grew faster in the summer compared to the spring, driven by consumer spending as well as investments in AI.
The previous quarter GDP grew at a 2.2% annual pace.
A big driver for GDP growth in the third quarter was the strong investments from AI companies, which continue to build out data centers and spend big money in developing the technology.
Meanwhile, consumer spending was another of the big drivers of GDP growth, led in part by higher-income Americans who are better able to withstand stubbornly high inflation.
Although consumer spending has been growing steadily, it has not spread out evenly across households, with lower-income Americans struggling more than high-earners.

title: US economy grew more than expected in 3rd quarter, government data shows
summary:
US economy grew more than expected in 3rd quarter, government data showsThe United States economy grew over the three months ending in September, according to a government report released on Thursday, which marked the final snapshot of the economy before next Tuesday's midterm elections.
Growth in the third quarter amounted to an acceleration from 2.2% annualized GDP growth in the previous quarter, as seen in Commerce Department data.
The performance in the third quarter also outpaced a 2.5% annualized rate recorded over the first three months of this year.
The central bank raised interest rates a quarter of a percentage point last month in an effort to battle back price woes.
Prices increased 3.7% in September compared to a year earlier, putting the inflation rate more than a percentage point above the Fed's target level of 2%, government data showed.

title: Stock market today: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 clobbered as October closes with brutal sell-off
summary:
The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) tumbled 2.8% as a tech-fueled sell-off intensified.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 1.2%, or over 650 points, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) dropped 2%.
For the month, the Dow gained 1.5%, while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 gave up gains, falling 5.2% and 1.2%, respectively.
October marked the worst month for the Nasdaq since March 2025.
Amazon shares fell 2%, while Alphabet continued to erase market value after its stock suffered its worst day in over 20 years.

title: What the Fed's interest rate decision means for your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
summary:
The national average interest rate on checking accounts has barely budged this year, remaining at 0.07%.
This is one category where rate shopping and subsequent increases in the Fed rate really pay off.
The federal funds rate doesn't directly determine federal student loan interest rates, but it can influence them indirectly.
Congress sets the federal student loan rates based on the 10-year Treasury note, adding a fixed margin each year.
When investors expect high inflation or strong economic growth, they demand higher yields, which can push federal student loan rates higher.

title: Scott Bessent says neocloud debt isn't problematic at all
summary:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent weighed in on the neocloud debt debate that recently rattled the AI trade, and he doesn't seem too concerned.
In a CNBC interview Wednesday, Bessent was asked about yields on some AI-related debt climbing into the double digits.
The neocloud industry, which includes players such as CoreWeave and Nebius, provides cloud computing services to AI customers.
The Roundhill Neocloud ETF, which invests in major neocloud players such as CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN, has fallen 24% over the past month.
He added that SpaceX would not be acquiring any neocloud companies.

title: Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Holdings is acquiring ADT for $7.6 billion
summary:
The Joshua Kushner-led Thrive Holdings is acquiring ADT in an all-cash deal valued at $7.6 billion.
The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027 and will take ADT private, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.
Joshua Kushner is the brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.
Thrive Holdings was founded last year, serving as an offshoot of Joshua Kushner’s venture capital firm Thrive Capital Management.
TechCrunch likens Thrive Holdings to a “private equity firm for AI,” as it purchases “traditional” businesses, like accounting and IT services, and applies AI to their workflows.

title: Rivian’s R2 is officially its best-selling vehicle
summary:
Rivian made $176 million in gross profit this quarter, a $152 million improvement compared to the same time last year.
Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle.
Earlier this month, Rivian reported a record sales quarter, with 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered.
But the company said that the R2 is now the “best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume,” outselling the R1T and R1S, as well as the Electric Delivery Van (EDV).
“We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter,” Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement, ahead of the company’s earnings call this afternoon.
